questions.q:
Let $y = {y}_{1} \left(x\right)$~and~$y = {y}_{2} \left(x\right)$~be~the~solution curves the~differential equation~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} =y + 7$ with initial~conditions~${y}_{1} \left($0\right) = 0$ and~{y}_{2}\left($0\right) = 1$ respectively. Then the curves~$y = ${y}_{1}\left($x\right)$ and~$y = {y}_{2} \left(x\right)$ intersect at

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have been given that$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 7 ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y + 7} = dx$

$⇒ ln | y + 7 | = x + c$

$⇒ | y + 7 | = k . e^{x}$

$⇒ y = k \cdot e^{x} - 7$

$⇒ {y}_{1} \left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ k = 7 ⇒ {y}_{1} \left($x\right) = $7\left($e^{x} - 1\right)$

$⇒ ${y}_{2}\left($0\right) = 1 ⇒ 1 = k - 7 ⇒ 8 = k$

$⇒ ${y}_{2}\left($x\right) = 8e^{x} - 7$

$⇒ ${y}_{1}\left($x\right) = ${y}_{2}\left($x\right) ⇒ 8e^{x} - 7 = 7e^{x} - 7$

Hence, No point of intersection.

This is the required option.

$

questions.q: If $\sin \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} | x | + \dfrac{α}{2}$ is the solution of the differential equation $xcos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = ycos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + x$ and $y ( 1 ) = \dfrac{π}{3}$, then ${α}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: \left(xcos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = ycos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + x$

$⇒ \cos \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\cos \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) + 1$

Putting, $y = vx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$⇒ \cos v\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = vcosv + 1$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v + \dfrac{1}{\cos v}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\cos v}$

$⇒ \left(\cos v\right)dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\cos v\right)dv = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \sin v = \log \left|x\right| + c$

$⇒ \sin \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log \left|x\right| + c$

Now, $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ \sin \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \log \left|1\right| + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{2} = c$

$⇒ \sin \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log \left|x\right| + \dfrac{3}{2}$

So, on comparing we get,

$⇒ \alpha = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ {α}^{2} = 3$

$

questions.q: Let slope of the tangent line to a curve at any point $P  \left(x, y\right)$ be given by \dfrac{xy^{2} + y}{x}.If the curve intersects the line $x + 2y = 4$ at $x = - 2$, then the value of $y$, for which the point  \left(3, y\right)$ lies on the curve, is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{xy^{2} + y}{x}$

$\dfrac{xdy - ydx}{y2} = xdx$

$- d\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = xdx$

$- \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{x2}{2} + c$

$∵$~Curve intersects the line~$x + 2y = 4$ at~$x = - 2 ⇒$ point of intersection is \left(- 2, 3\right)$.~

$∴$~Curve passes through \left(- 2, 3\right)$.~

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = 2 + c ⇒ c = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- x}{y} = \dfrac{x2}{2} - \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now put \left(3, y\right)$~we get,~

$⇒ \dfrac{- 3}{y} = \dfrac{19}{6}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{- 18}{19}$

$

questions.q: Let $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{ax - by + a}{bx + cy + a}$, where $a, b, c$ are constants. represent a circle passing through the point  \left(2, 5\right)$. Then the shortest distance of the point~  \left(11, 6\right)$ from this circle is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let equation of circle is

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$

Differentiating above equation w.r.t~$x$~we get,~

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(2x + 2g\right)\left(2y + 2f\right)$

Now, comparing with~\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{ax - by + a}{bx + cy + a}

We get,~$b = 0, a = - 2, c = 2$

$⇒ - 2g = - 2 ⇒ g = 1$

Also,~$2f = - 2$

So,~$f = - 1$

Now circle will be

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x - 2y + c = 0$

its passes through~ \left($2, 5\right)$

which will give~$c = - 23$

so circle will be~$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x - 2y - 23 = 0$

centre~$C = \left(-$1, 1\right)$

and radius~$5$

Now~$P$~is~ \left(11, 6\right)$

So minimum distance of~$P$~from circle will be~$= \sqrt{\left(11 + 1\right)2 + \left(6 - 1\right)2} -5$

$= 13 - 5 = 8$

questions.q: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $xdy = \left(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} + y\right)dx, x > 0$, intersect the line $x = 1$ at $y = 0$ and the line $x = 2$ at $y = \alpha$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$xdy = \left(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} + y\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy - ydx = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{x2} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{y2}{x2}} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{1 + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{1 + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \ln \left(\dfrac{y}{x} + \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)2 + 1}\right) = \ln x + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{y + \sqrt{y^{2} + x^{2}}}{x} = cx$

$⇒ y + \sqrt{y^{2} + x^{2}} = cx^{2}$

Now given when~$x = 1, y = 0 ⇒ 0 + 1 = c ⇒ c = 1$

So equation of curve is~$y + \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} = x^{2}$

Now at~$x = 2, y = \alpha$

So putting the value in curve we get,~$2 + \sqrt{4 + {α}^{2}} = 4$

$⇒ 4 + {α}^{2} = 16 + {α}^{2} = 8\alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(x^2+1\right) y^{\prime}-2 x y=\left(x^4+2 x^2+1\right) \cos x$, $y(0)=1$. Then $\int_{-3}^3 y(x) d x$ is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(x^2+1\right) \frac{d y}{d x}-2 x y=\left(x^4+2 x^2+1\right) \cos x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}-\left(\frac{2 x}{x^2+1}\right) y=\frac{\left(x^2+1\right)^2 \cos x}{\mathrm{cx}^2+1}=\left(\mathrm{x}^2+1\right) \cos x \\ & \text { (Linear D.E) } \\ & P=\frac{-2 x}{x^2+1}, Q=\left(x^2+1\right) \cos x \\ & \text { I.F }=e^{\int P d x}=e^{\int \frac{-2 x}{x^2+1} d x}=\frac{1}{x^2+1} \\ & y \cdot \frac{1}{x^2+1}=\int\left(x^2+1\right) \cos x \cdot \frac{1}{x^2+1} d x \\ & \frac{y}{x^2+1}=\sin x+c \Rightarrow y \cos =1 \Rightarrow c=1 \\ & y=\left(x^2+1\right)(\sin x+1) \\ & \int_{-3}^3 y d x=\int_{-3}^3\left(x^2+1\right)(\sin x+1) \\ & d x=\int_{-3}^3 x^2 \sin x+x^2 \sin x+1 d x \\ & \Rightarrow \int_{-3}^3 x^2 \sin x d x+\int_{-3}^3 x^2 d x+\int_{-3}^3 \sin x d x+\int_{-3}^3 1 d x \\ & =0+18+0+6=24
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\sqrt{1 + x^{2} + y^{2} + x^{2}y^{2}} + xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$& (where C is a constant& of integration)
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)\left(1 + y^{2}\right)} + xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Integrating,

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{2y}{2\sqrt{1 + y^{2}}}\right)dy = - ∫ \left(\dfrac{1 + x^{2}}{x\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}\right)dx$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + y^{2}} = - ∫ \dfrac{x}{1 + x^{2}}dx - ∫ \dfrac{x}{x^{2}\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}dx$

Put~$\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = t ⇒ x^{2} = t^{2} - 1$~to solve RHS~2nd integration,~

$⇒ \sqrt{1 + y^{2}} = - \sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - ∫ \dfrac{t}{\left(t^{2} - 1\right)t}dt$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + y^{2}} + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = - ∫ \dfrac{1}{t^{2} - 1}dt$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + y^{2}} + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} + 1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - 1}\right] + C$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$~be the solution of the differential equation $( x^{2} – 3y^{2} ) dx + 3xydy = 0, y ( 1 ) = 1$. Then~$6y^{2}  \left(e\right)& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equation is:

$( x^{2} – 3y^{2} ) dx + 3xydy = 0$

We can re-write equation as

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(x^{2} - 3y^{2}\right)3xy$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{x}{y}$~ ....(1)

Put~$y = vx$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

Equation (1) can be written as

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v - \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{1}{v} ⇒ vdv = - \dfrac{1}{3x}$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\dfrac{v2}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left(x\right) + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{y2}{2x^{2}} = \dfrac{- 1}{3}\ln \left(x\right) + c$~ ~ ~ ~ .....(2)

$∵ y\left(1\right) = 1$~ ~ ~(given)

$∴ c = \dfrac{1}{2}$~ ~ ~ ~(from equation 2)

Equation (2) can be written as

$\dfrac{y2}{2x^{2}} = \dfrac{- 1}{3}\ln \left(x\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ y^{2} = \dfrac{- 2}{3}x^{2}\ln \left(x\right) + x^{2}$

Now~$y^{2} ( e ) = \dfrac{- 2}{3}e^{2}\ln \left(e\right) + e^{2} = \dfrac{- 2}{3}e^{2} + e^{2} = \dfrac{e2}{3}$

$⇒ 6y^{2} ( e ) = 2e^{2}$

questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 0 . 5P - 450$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dp}{P - 900} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{2}$

$⇒ {In\left|P\left(t\right) - 900\right|}_{0}^{t} = {\dfrac{t}{2}}_{0}^{t}$

$⇒ In\left|P\left(t\right) - 900\right| - In\left|P\left(0\right) - 900\right| = \dfrac{t}{2}$

$⇒ In\left|P\left(t\right) - 900\right| - In\left|50\right| = \dfrac{t}{2}$

for $P\left(t\right) = 0$

$⇒ In\left|\dfrac{900}{50}\right| = \dfrac{t}{2} ⇒ t = 2In18$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation \left(x + 1\right)y^{'} - y = e^{3x}\left(x + 1\right)2$, with $y  \left(0\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}.$~Then, the point $x = - \dfrac{4}{3}$~for the curve $y = y\left(x\right)$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(x + 1\right)dy - ydx = e^{3x}\left(x + 1\right)2dx$

$\dfrac{\left(x + 1\right)dy - ydx}{( x + 1{)}^{2}} = e^{3x}dx$

$d\left(\dfrac{y}{x + 1}\right) = e^{3x}dx$

On integration, we get

$\dfrac{y}{x + 1} = \dfrac{e3x}{3} + C$

Given~$y\left(0\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

So~$C = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{ \left(x + 1\right)e^{3x}}{3}$

\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{e3x}{3}\left($3x + 4\right)$

\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} =$e^{3x} \left(3x + 5\right)$

Clearly, $x = \dfrac{- 4}{3}$is~a point of local minima as~ \left(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right)$x = $\dfrac{- 4}{3}$< 0$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\sec y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}+2 x \sin y=x^3 \cos y, y(1)=0$. Then $y(\sqrt{3})$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x \sin y \text { \sec y }=x^3 \cos y \text { \sec y } \\ & \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x \tan y=x^3 \\ & \operatorname{\tan y}=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x} \\ & \frac{d t}{d x}+2 x t=x^3, \text { If }=e^{\int 2 x d x}=e^{x^2} \\ & t x^{x^2}=\int x^3 \cdot e^{x^2} d x+c \\ & x^2=Z \Rightarrow t \cdot e^Z=\frac{1}{2} \int e^Z \cdot Z d Z=\frac{1}{2}\left[e^Z \cdot Z-e^Z\right]+c \\ & 2 \tan y=\left(x^2-1\right)+2 e^{-x^2} \\ & y(1)=0 \Rightarrow c=0 \Rightarrow y(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
f^{'}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1} \left(sec x + tan x\right) = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 + sin x}{cos x}\right) = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 - \cos \left(\dfrac{π}{2} +x\right)}${\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2} +$x\right)}\right)

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2\sin^{2} \left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2sin $\left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$\cos \left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{x}{2})})$

$⇒ \left(f^{'} \left(x\right)\right)dx = \left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{x}{2})$dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{π}{4}$x + $\dfrac{x2}{4} +$c$

$∵ f\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

So,~$f\left(1\right) = $\dfrac{\pi + 1}{4}

$

questions.q: The solution curve of the differential equation $y\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}x - \log_{\mathrm{e}}y + 1\right), x > 0, y > 0$ passing through the point $( e, 1 )$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $y\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}x - \log_{\mathrm{e}}y + 1\right), x > 0, y > 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) \left[\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) +$1\right]$

Putting, $x = vy$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dx}{dy} =$v + $y\dfrac{dv}{dx}

$⇒ v + $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = $\left(\dfrac{vy}{y}) \left[\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{vy}{y}\right) +$1\right]$

$⇒ v + $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} =$v \left[\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left($v\right) + 1\right]$

$⇒ v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy} =v\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(v\right) + v$

$⇒ $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} =$v\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(v\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dv}{v\log_{\mathrm{e}}v} = \dfrac{dy}{y}

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{dv}{v\log_{\mathrm{e}}v} =$∫ $\dfrac{dy}{y}

Putting, $\log_{\mathrm{e}}v = t$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dv}{v} =$dt$

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{dt}{t} =$∫ $\dfrac{dy}{y}

$⇒ \log t = \log y + c$

$⇒ \log \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{x}{y}\right) =\log y + c$

Using point \left(e, 1\right)$

$⇒ \log \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}e\right) = \log \left(1\right) + c$

$⇒ c = 0$

$⇒ \log \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{x}{y}\right) =\log y$

$⇒ \left|\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{x}{y}\right| =y$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable function defined on $R$ such that $f\left(0\right) = 1, f^{'}\left(0\right) = 2$ and $f^{'}\left(x\right) \ne 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R} .$~If \left|$\begin{cases}f\left(x\right) & f^{'}\left(x\right) \\ f^{'}\left(x\right) & f^{''}  \left(x\right)\end{cases}$\right| = 0,$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R},$ then the value of $f\left(1\right)$ lies in the interval$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& \left|$\begin{cases}f\left(x\right) & f^{'}\left(x\right) \\ f^{'}\left(x\right) & f^{' '}\left(x\right)\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)f^{' '}\left(x\right) - \left(f^{'}\left(x\right)\right)2 = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{f^{' '}\left(x\right)}{f^{'}\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{f^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}$

On integrating both side, we get

$\ln \left(f^{'} \left(x\right)\right) = lnf \left($x\right) + lnc$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = cf \left($x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{f^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} =$c$

Again integrating, we get

lnf\left($x\right) = cx + {k}_{1}$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = ke^{cx}$

Since,~f\left($0\right) = 1 = k$

Therefore,~$f^{'}\left($0\right) = c = 2$

Now,~$f \left(x\right) = e^{2x}$

Hence,~$f\left(1\right) = e^{2} \in \left(6, 9\right)$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation can be written as

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2y}{x} = x$ , which is a linear differential equation.

If $= e^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = e^{2\ln x} = x^{2}$

Solution is

$⇒ y . x^{2} = \dfrac{x^{4}}{4} + c$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 3y^{2}}{3x^{2} + y^{2}}\right), y\left(1\right) = 0$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Differential equation,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 3y^{2}}{3x^{2} + y^{2}}\right) \text{ and } y\left(1\right) = 0$

Now let~$y = vx$

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - \left(\dfrac{1 + 3v^{2}}{3 + v^{2}}\right)

$⇒ x$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - \dfrac{\left(v + 1\right)3}{3 + v^{2}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left(3 + v^{2}\right)dv}{\left(v + 1\right)3} + \dfrac{dx}{x} =$0$

$⇒ ∫ $\dfrac{4dv}{\left(v + 1\right)3} +$∫ $\dfrac{dv}{v + 1} -$∫ $\dfrac{2dv}{\left(v + 1\right)2} +$∫ $\dfrac{dx}{x} =$0$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 2}{\left(v + 1\right)2} +$\ln \left|$v + 1\right| + $\dfrac{2}{v + 1} +$\ln \left|$x\right| = c$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 2x^{2}}{\left(x + y\right)2} +$\ln \left|\dfrac{x + y}{x}\right| + \dfrac{2x}{x + y} +$\ln \left|$x\right| = c$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2xy}{\left(x + y\right)2} +$\ln \left|$x + y\right| = c$

$∵ y\left($1\right) = 0$

$∴ c = 0$, as $x = 1, y = 0$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2xy}{\left(x + y\right)2} +$\ln \left|$x + y\right| = 0$

questions.q: Let a smooth curve $y = f  \left(x\right)$~be such that the slope of the tangent at any point~  \left(x, y\right)$ on it is directly proportional to  \left(\dfrac{- y}{x}\right).$If the curve passes through the points \left(1, 2\right)$ and  \left($8, 1\right)$, then \left|y\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)|& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} ∝ \dfrac{- y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- Ky}{x}$~(where $K$~is proportionality constant)

Now integrating both side,~

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} = - K ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \ln \left|y\right| = - Kln \left|$x\right| + C$

If the above equation satisfy~\left($1, 2\right)$

$⇒ \ln 2 = - K \times0 + C ⇒ C = \ln 2$

So,~$\ln \left|$y\right| = - Kln \left|$x\right| + \ln 2$

Now it also passes through~\left($8, 1\right)$

$⇒ \ln 1 = - Kln8 + \ln 2 ⇒ K = $\dfrac{1}{3}

So, equation becomes~\ln \left|$y\right| = - $\ddfrac{1}{3}\ln \left|x\right| + \ln 2$

So, at~$x = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$⇒ \ln \left|y\right| = - $\d$dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left(\dfrac{1}{8}) +\ln 2 = 2\ln 2$

$⇒ \left|$y\right| = 4$

$

questions.q:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation
$x\left(x^2+e^x\right) d y+\left(e^x(x-2) y-x^3\right) d x=0, x \gt 0$ passing through the point $(1,0)$. Then $y(2)$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x\left(x^2+e^x\right) d y+\left(e^x(x-2) y-x^3\right) d x=0 \\ & x\left(x^2+e^x\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+e^x(x-2) y=x^3 \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{e^x(x-2)}{x\left(x^2+e^x\right)} y=\frac{x^2}{x^2+e^x} \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{e^x(x-2)}{x\left(x^2+e^x\right)} d x}=e^{\int \frac{e^x\left(\frac{1}{x^2}-\frac{2}{x^2}\right) d x}{\left(1+\frac{e^x}{x^2}\right)} d x}\end{aligned}$
Let $1+\frac{e^x}{x^2}=t \Rightarrow \frac{x^2 e^x-e^x 2 x}{x^4} d x=d t$
$\Rightarrow \text { I.F. } \mathrme^{\ln \left(1+\frac{\mathrm{e}^2}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)}=1+\frac{\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{x}^2}$
Now $y\left(1+\frac{e^x}{x^2}\right)=\int \frac{x^2}{x^2+e^x} \cdot \frac{x^2+e^x}{x^2} d x+C$
$y\left(1+\frac{e^x}{x^2}\right)=x+C$
Passing through $(1,0)$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow C=-1 \\ & y=\frac{x-1}{1+\frac{e^x}{x^2}} \\ & y(2)=\frac{1}{1+\frac{e^2}{4}}=\frac{4}{4+e^2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $x = x ( t )$ and $y = y ( t )$ be solutions of the differential equations $\dfrac{dx}{dt} + ax = 0$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt} + by = 0$ respectively, $a, b \in R$. Given that $x ( 0 ) = 2; y ( 0 ) = 1$ and $3y ( 1 ) = 2x ( 1 )$, the value of $t$, for which $x ( t ) = y ( t )$, is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\dfrac{dx}{dt} + ax = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{x} = - adt$

Integrating both sides,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x} = - a ∫ dt$

$⇒ log | x | = - at + c$

At $t = 0, x = 2$

$⇒ \log 2 = 0 + c$

$⇒ \log x = - at + \log 2$

$⇒ \log x - \log 2 = - at$

$⇒ \log \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = - at$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} = e^{- at}$

$⇒ x = 2e^{- at} . . . ( i )$

It is also given that, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} + by = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} = - bdt$

$⇒ log | y | = - bt + \lambda$

At, $t = 0, y = 1$

$⇒ 0 = 0 + \lambda$

$⇒ y = e^{- bt} . . . ( ii )$

According to question,

$3y ( 1 ) = 2x ( 1 )$

$⇒ 3e^{- b} = 2 \left(2e^{- a}\right)$

$⇒ e^{a - b} = $\dfrac{4}{3}

$\text{For}x \left(t\right) = y \left(t\right)$

$⇒ 2e^{- at} = e^{- bt}$

$⇒ 2 = e^{( a - b ) t}$

$⇒ 2 = $\left(\dfrac{4}{3})t$

$⇒ $\log \left($2\right) = t $\timeslog\left(\dfrac{4}{3})$

$⇒ log\dfrac{4}{3}2 = t

$

questions.q: Let $y=f(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}+\frac{x y}{x^2-1}=\frac{x^6+4 x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}},-1 \lt x \lt 1$ such that $f(0)=0$. If $6 \int_{-1 / 2}^{1 / 2} f(x) \mathrm{d} x=2 \pi-\alpha$ then $\alpha^2$ is equal to _______ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: I.F. $\mathrme^{-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 \mathrm{x}}{1-\mathrm{x}^2} \mathrm{dx}}=\mathrme^{-\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(1-\mathrm{x}^2\right)}=\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^2}y \times \sqrt{1-x^2}=\int\left(x^6+4 x\right) d x=\frac{x^7}{7}+2 x^2+c$ Given $y(0)=0 \Rightarrow c=0y=\frac{\frac{x^7}{7}+2 x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$ Now, $6 \int_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{\frac{x^7}{7}+2 \mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^2}} \mathrm{dx}=6 \int_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{2 \mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^2}} \mathrm{dx}$\begin{aligned} & =24 \int_0^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} d x \\ & \text { Put } x=\sin \theta \\ & d x=\cos \theta d \theta \\ & =24 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} \cos \theta d \theta \\ & =24 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\left(\frac{1-\cos 2 \theta}{2}\right) d \theta=12\left[\theta-\frac{\sin 2 \theta}{2}\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \\ & =12\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) \\ & =2 \pi-3 \sqrt{3} \\ & \alpha^2=(3 \sqrt{3})^2=27\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: If& $y = y \left(x\right), y \in \left[$0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)~is the solution of the~differential equation~\sec y\dfrac{dy}{dx} -\sin \left($x + y\right) - \sin \left(x - y\right) = 0,$~with~$y\left(0\right) = 0$,~then~$5y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)$& is equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\sec y\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \sin \left(x + y\right) - \sin \left(x - y\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sec y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\sin x \cos y$

$⇒ \sec^{2}ydy = 2sinxdx$

$⇒ ∫ \sec^{2}ydy = ∫ 2sinxdx$

$⇒ \tan y = - 2\cos x + c$

Given,~$y\left(0\right) = 0$

So,~$0 = - 2\cos 0 + c$

$⇒ c = 2$

So, the particular solution is~

$\tan y = - 2\cos x + 2$

at~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}, \tan y = - 2cos\dfrac{π}{2} + 2$

$⇒ \tan y = 2 ⇒ \sec^{2}y = 5$

Here, differentiate both sides of~$\tan y = - 2\cos x + 2,$~we get,

$\sec^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\sin x$

At~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$5\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

$⇒ 5$\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$2$

$

questions.q: Let $y = y \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\sec^{2}xdx + \left(e^{2y}\tan^{2}x + \tan x\right)dy = 0,0 < x < $\dfrac{π}{2},$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =0$. If $y\left(\dfrac{π}{6}) = \alpha,then $e^{8\alpha} is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\sec^{2}xdx + \left(e^{2y}\tan^{2}x + \tan x\right)dy = 0,$

$⇒ \sec^{2}\dfrac{dx}{dy} + e^{2y}\tan^{2}x + \tan x = 0$

Now, let $\tan x = t ⇒ \sec^{2}x\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{dt}{dy}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} + e^{2y} \times t^{2} + t = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} + t = - t^{2} . e^{2y}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{t2}\dfrac{dt}{dy} + \dfrac{1}{t} = - e^{2y}$

Now, taking $\dfrac{1}{t} = u ⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{t2}\dfrac{dt}{dy} = \dfrac{du}{dy}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- du}{dy} + u = - e^{2y}$

$⇒ \dfrac{du}{dy} - u = e^{2y}$

Now, finding an integrating factor $IF = e^{- ∫ dy} = e^{- y}$

So, the solution is given by,

$ue^{- y} = ∫ e^{- y} \times e^{2y}dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{e- y}{t} = e^{y} + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\tan x} \times e^{- y} = e^{y} + c$

Now, using the given condition at $x = \dfrac{π}{4}, y = 0$ we get,

$⇒ c = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\tan x} = e^{2y}$

Now, putting the value $x = \dfrac{π}{6}, y = \alpha$ we get,

$e^{2\alpha} = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ e^{8\alpha} = 9$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x+y+2)^2 d x=d y, y(0)=-2$. Let the maximum and minimum values of the function $y=y(x)$ in  \left[0, \frac{\pi}{3}\right]$ be $\alpha$ and $\beta$, respectively. If $(3 \alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=\gamma+\delta \sqrt{3}, \gamma, \delta \in \mathbb{Z}$, then $\gamma+\delta$ equals ______$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\frac{d y}{d x}=(x+y+2)^2$ ...(1) $y(0)=-2$
Let $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+2=\mathrm{v}1+\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}$ from (1) $\frac{d v}{d x}=1+v^2$\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{d v}{1+v^2}=\int d x \\ & \tan ^{-1}(v)=x+C \\ & \tan ^{-1}(x+y+2)=x+C \\ & \text { at } x=0 y=-2 \Rightarrow C=0 \end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+2)=\mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{y}=\tan \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}-2 \\ & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\tan \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}-2, \mathrm{x} \in\left[0, \frac{\pi}{3}\right] \end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime}(x)=\sec ^2 x-1 \gt 0 \Rightarrow f(x) \uparrow \\ & f_{\min }=f(0)=-2=\beta \\ & f_{\max }=f\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi}{3}-2=\alpha \end{aligned}$$ now $(3 \alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=\gamma+\delta \sqrt{3}$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(3 \alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=(3 \sqrt{3}-6)^2+4 \\ & \gamma+\delta \sqrt{3}=67-36 \sqrt{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \gamma=67 \text { and } \delta=-36 \Rightarrow \gamma+\delta=31 \end{aligned}$$
